+```
+
+Every body line is prefixed with `>` and a space, so message text cannot forge a frame of its own.
+
+### Tool and CLI
+
+- Plugin tool `aidevops_sessions` with `action: list | show | send | ask | reply | inbox | notify-when-idle`. `list` returns at most 20 compact rows (~25 tokens each) sorted by repo match, then activity. Schema target ≤150 tokens. Direct (not behind `aidevops_on_demand`) because discoverability is the point; revisit after usage evidence. Interactive processes only: headless workers do not get the tool, which saves its schema on every worker request.
+- CLI `aidevops sessions [list|show|send|ask|inbox|outbox]` via `session-bus-helper.sh`, a thin wrapper over `session-bus-cli.mjs`, which shares `session-bus-store.mjs` with the plugin. Gives the user a terminal view of what every session is doing and gives chat gateways (Phase 3) one stable entry point.
+- Guidance: `.agents/AGENTS.md` is at its 24,000-byte ratchet (23,993 bytes on 2026-11-07), so the tool description carries the "never ask the user to relay" rule, which is loaded with every request anyway. Details live in `reference/session-bus.md`, which replaces `reference/mailbox.md` content when Phase 4 is approved.
+
+### Sidebar "Messages" section
+
+Owner request: a "Messages" section in the right sidebar, under "Prompts". This build ships it for OpenCode 1.x (`v1-tui/tui.tsx`, slot order 60, after Prompts at 50) through `tui-messages.mjs`. OpenCode 2 is a follow-up: the V2 server plugin (`v2.mjs`) does not run the bus yet, so a V2 sidebar would never show traffic. The TUI reads the current root session's bus files directly, with no server round trip, every 5s. It shows the latest 6 messages, newest first: `← handle: text` for received, `→ handle: text` for sent, `•` while undelivered. The header collapses like Prompts. The section is hidden when the session has no traffic. Disable it with `AIDEVOPS_TUI_MESSAGES=false`. Toasts are the only notification (owner answer 2): no bell or OS notification.
+
+### Origin, outbox and chat-gateway wiring
+
+Every message carries `from.origin`:
+
+| Origin | Producer | Trust | Can wake? |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `opencode` | `aidevops_sessions` tool in a root session | Peer agent; no user authority | `ask`, own-`ask` `reply`, `idle-notice` |
+| `cli` | `aidevops sessions send/ask` from a shell | Local user's shell, but unauthenticated text in a session | Same as `opencode` |
+| `chat:<app>:<channel>` | Future gateway (SimpleX, Matrix, Buzz) via the CLI | External; framed as unverified chat input | Never in this build. Wakes need a verified owner entity and a per-session opt-in (Phase 3) |
+
+A `reply` to a message whose origin is `chat:*` is also written to `outbox/<app>/<msgID>.json`. Gateways read it with `aidevops sessions outbox <app> --json` and acknowledge with `--ack <msgID>`. This build ships the outbox writer and reader. It ships no gateway.
+
+Chat-app wiring kept open for Phase 3 (owner turn 3: long-running sessions per channel and per-task sessions from mobile, for remote work and `opencode serve`):
+
+- **Channel → session binding:** `bindings/<app>/<channel>.json` maps a chat channel to one root session ID. A gateway resolves the binding and sends to that session through the inbox, so the same delivery, framing and limits apply. If the bound session is gone, the gateway reports that to the channel. It never silently retargets.
+- **Per-task launch:** a gateway creates a session on an `opencode serve` instance (the existing Matrix `POST /session` path), titles it `Issue #N: …`, writes the binding, then sends the task text through the inbox. Presence then lists it like any other session.
+- **Remote `opencode serve`:** the bus is local files, so a gateway runs on the same host as the server. A remote host needs its own gateway. There is no cross-host bus.
+
+### Safety and abuse limits
+
+- Peer messages never carry user authority (frame above; same rule as tool output). They cannot approve merges, releases, destructive operations, secret access, settings or scope changes, and cannot answer a pending permission prompt.
+- Loop control: `hops` increments when a session sends while handling a bus-woken turn; messages with `hops ≥ 3` are delivered but never wake. Each session accepts at most 6 wakes per hour; extra wake-eligible messages wait for the next turn. Replies never auto-trigger replies.
+- Rate limits: a sender may send at most 10 messages per minute; an inbox holds at most 50 pending messages (sender gets an error beyond that).
+- Headless workers (`opencode run`, `kind: headless`) are listed read-only and reject `send`/`ask`.
+- Same-user, same-machine trust boundary (filesystem permissions 700/600). No network listener is added.
+- Retention: delivered and undeliverable messages are pruned after 7 days; presence records disappear with their process.
+
+### Context, storage and reliability costs
+
+| Dimension | Estimate | Basis |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Storage | presence ≈1KB × live sessions (~25 ⇒ ~25KB); messages ≤2.5KB each, 7-day retention ⇒ <1MB at 50 messages/day | file sizes above |
+| Context when unused | ~150 tokens of tool schema per request (prompt-cached); zero injected text | tool schema budget |
+| Context per message | ≤2,000 chars (~500 tokens) + ~80-token frame, persisted once | cap |
+| `list` | ≤20 rows, ~500 tokens | cap |
+| CPU/IO | one 5s inbox `readdir` per process; presence writes ≤1 per 10s | throttle |
+| Reliability | atomic rename; at-least-once + ID dedupe; offline recipient ⇒ sender told at send time and message kept 7 days; process crash ⇒ undelivered files remain and are delivered when the session resumes in any process | design |
+
+## Chat-app gateways (SimpleX, Matrix, Buzz) — design only
+
+Owner requirement: aidevops must also be usable from chat apps. Current state (verified by reading the integrations):
+
+| App | Today | Reaches a live interactive session? |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Matrix (`matrix-bot.mjs.template`) | `!ai` → creates a fresh session on an OpenCode server (`POST /session`, `/session/{id}/message`) per room+actor, or `runner-helper.sh`; entity-aware context via `entity-helper.sh`/`memory.db` | No |
+| SimpleX (`simplex-bot/`) | Bun bot spawns aidevops CLI/`runner-helper.sh`; `/run` needs approval | No |
+| Buzz (`team-interface-buzz*`, t18883/GH#36976) | Read-only adapter; restricted `opencode acp` conversation overlays | No |
+| `mail-helper-transport.sh` SimpleX/Matrix relay | Reads `spool/simplex/*.envelope`; no live producer found | No |
+
+The bus gives every gateway one contract instead of three bespoke paths:
+
+1. **Read (cheap, no LLM):** `aidevops sessions list --json` answers "what is running / what is session X doing" directly from presence. Safe default for a verified owner identity; titles, repos and branches can be private, so group rooms get redacted rows.
+2. **Send:** `aidevops sessions send --to <target> --origin chat:<app>:<entity-id> --text-file <path>`. Chat-origin messages are a distinct trust profile (`team-interface-trust.md`): actor identity, content provenance, attachment risk and requested capability are evaluated separately; content is scanned with `prompt-guard-helper.sh scan`; delivery framing says "from chat user …, unverified/verified" and carries no owner authority.
+3. **Wake policy:** chat messages never wake a session unless the actor is a verified owner entity (`entity-helper.sh` `--verified` channel link) **and** the target session has opted in. Even then the capability is conversation only.
+4. **Replies back:** a session replying to a chat-origin message writes to `session-bus/outbox/<gateway>/`; the gateway polls its outbox and posts to the room/contact, applying its existing leak detection (SimpleX `leak-detector.ts`) before sending.

+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Plugin loads in `opencode serve` (desktop path) | Go | Spike plugin `init` logged from a `serve` process; in-process client exposes `session.promptAsync`, `session.prompt`, `tui.showToast` |

+| `tool.execute.after` appends to `output.output` | Go | Text persisted in the tool result; the model used it and treated it as data |

+| --- | --- |

+| Next-turn delivery | Info messages waiting for idle A arrived as synthetic parts on A's next user turn, in batches of 5. |

+| Rate limit | 10 shell sends in a minute succeeded; the 11th was refused (`at most 10 messages per minute per sender`). |
+| `SIGKILL` | After `kill -9` of the server, both presence files remained on disk. The next `list` dropped both sessions and removed the files. |
+| Toast | No `session-bus` warnings in the server log. `serve` has no TUI, so the toast itself was not seen. |
+| Sidebar | Not verified live; needs a V1 TUI session. |

+
+- A session created over the API had no status event, so it stayed `unknown` and could not be woken. `session.created` now marks a root session idle unless a status event already arrived.
+- `reply` accepted any received message as `re`, so sessions could trade replies until the hop limit stopped wakes. It now accepts only asks.
+- An isolated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` run cannot resolve `@opencode-ai/plugin` from a repo worktree, so no aidevops tools register (`tool-schema.mjs` logs `V1 schemas unavailable`). This affects test setups only. The deployed plugin has its own `node_modules`.
+
+## Problem
+
+Agents often need to know what parallel OpenCode sessions are doing ("is anyone working on #NNN?", "has the other session merged its PR?"), or to tell another session something. Today the user is the relay: the agent asks the user to copy text between terminals.
+
+The old mailbox (`mail-helper.sh`, `reference/mailbox.md`) was meant to solve this but does not work in practice:

+| --- | --- |

+| No delivery hook in the OpenCode plugin | A message never reaches a running session. |

+

+
+1. **Presence:** any session (and the user, from a shell) can list live interactive OpenCode sessions with repo, worktree, branch, linked issue/PR, busy/idle state and current task. Answering "what are the others doing" costs one tool call, no message, no other session's tokens.
+2. **Messages:** a session can `send` information, `ask` a question that expects a reply, `reply`, and `notify-when-idle` on another session.
+3. **Delivery without the user relaying:** messages reach a busy session at its next tool result, an idle session at its next turn, and an `ask` may wake an idle session (owner decision 1a).
+4. **Bounded cost:** no daemon, no database, small files, zero context cost when nothing is sent.
+5. **Safe by construction:** peer messages are never user authority.
+

+
+- Claude Code, Codex or other runtime interop.
+- Messaging headless workers. Workers appear in presence (read-only) but cannot be messaged; they keep their issue/PR as the only communication channel.
+- Cross-machine delivery. Chat-app gateways (below) are the remote path, designed here and built later.
+- Removing the old mailbox. That needs a separate owner decision (Phase 4).

+
+Everything lives under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/session-bus/` (mode 700, files 600):

+```text
+session-bus/
+  presence/<sessionID>.json          # one per live root session, written by its owning process
+  inbox/<sessionID>/<ts>-<msgID>.json  # pending messages, one file each
+  inbox/<sessionID>/delivered/...    # moved here after delivery; pruned after 7 days
+  sent/<sessionID>/<ts>-<msgID>.json   # sender's copy: rate limit, sidebar, pending-ask summary
+  subs/<sessionID>/<subscriberID>.json # notify-when-idle subscriptions (one-shot)
+  outbox/<app>/<msgID>.json          # replies to chat-origin messages, for gateways (Phase 3)
+  bindings/<app>/<channel>.json      # channel → session (Phase 3; reserved, not written yet)
+```
+
+- Delivery claims a message by renaming it into `delivered/`. Exactly one process wins the rename, so two processes holding the same session cannot both deliver it.
+
+- All writes are temp-file + `rename` (atomic on the same filesystem), the same pattern as `db-activity-heartbeat.mjs` `write()`.
+- Message IDs are random; delivery is at-least-once with dedupe by ID in the recipient.

body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Report set-to-empty bus variables as set.** If either variable exists with an empty value, `${VAR:-}` makes the summary report `set=no`. The requested set/unset diagnostic then cannot distinguish an empty assignment from an absent variable. Use `${VAR+x}` to test whether each variable exists.
Proposed change

```diff --- "a/.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh" +++ "b/.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh" @@ -276,8 +276,8 @@ # Print set/unset booleans for the session-bus environment; never values. _dlw_systemd_bus_env_summary() { local xdg_set="no" dbus_set="no" - [[ -z "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-}" ]] || xdg_set="yes" - [[ -z "${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:-}" ]] || dbus_set="yes" + [[ -z "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR+x}" ]] || xdg_set="yes" + [[ -z "${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS+x}" ]] || dbus_set="yes" printf 'xdg_runtime_dir_set=%s dbus_session_bus_address_set=%s' "$xdg_set" "$dbus_set" return 0 } ```
Committable suggestion

> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion [[ -z "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR+x}" ]] || xdg_set="yes" [[ -z "${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS+x}" ]] || dbus_set="yes" ```

Pass the real `post_type` (`'page'` or the CPT) and `'post_status' => 'any'`, match with `'post_name__in' => array( $slug )` instead of `name` (which can hide matches), use `get_page_by_path( $path, OBJECT, 'page' )` (full `parent/child` path for child pages), query `$wpdb->posts` by `post_name` and `post_type`, or run `wp post list --post_type=page --name=<slug> --post_status=any --format=ids`. `'any'` excludes trash, but a trashed post's slug gets a `__trashed` suffix, so it does not block reuse. `'any'` also excludes `inherit`, `auto-draft` and custom statuses registered with `exclude_from_search`, yet those records can still occupy a slug; where they matter, pass an explicit `post_status` list or use the `$wpdb->posts` lookup. Pages and hierarchical CPTs share slugs with same-parent attachments, so include `'attachment'` in `post_type` when that collision matters. For these hierarchical guards, also pass `'post_parent' => $parent_id` to `get_posts()` or constrain `post_parent` to the target parent ID in the `$wpdb->posts` lookup (use `0` for top-level pages); this preserves same-parent collisions without rejecting slugs used under other parents.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Do not rely on `command -p -v git` alone.** `command -p` searches only the system default path. On NixOS or any host where Git is only on the caller `PATH`, `check=True` raises `CalledProcessError` and the whole module fails at import. `command -v` can also print a bare name for a builtin or function, so the result may not be an absolute path. Use `shutil.which("git")` against the caller `PATH`. Reject the aidevops wrapper, and raise a clear error if Git is not found. This also removes the shell call, which the `ast-grep` hint flags. That flag is a false positive here because the command is constant.

+---
+description: Triage and recovery for macOS login-password rejections, Recovery-mode password resets, set-aside login keychains, and keychain-stored app data
+mode: subagent
+---
+
+<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
+<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
+
+# macOS Account and Login-Keychain Recovery
+
+<!-- AI-CONTEXT-START -->
+
+## Quick Reference
+
+- **Use when:** a correct Mac login password is rejected; a password was reset
+  in Recovery; a `login_renamed_N.keychain-db` appears; keychain prompts loop;
+  agent sessions lose ssh, `gh`, signed commits or Chrome; app data stored in
+  the keychain (VPN tunnels, tokens) disappears; an unexpected screen-sharing
+  indicator needs explaining.
+- **Restart first:** if `id -un` prints a number, or ssh/`gh`/signing fail
+  while plain HTTPS works, macOS user lookup is broken. Tell the user to
+  restart; do not poll or retry for hours (GH#37260).
+- **Passwords:** the user types every password at a Terminal or system prompt.
+  Never ask for one in chat, never echo, store or log one.
+- **Copies only:** test, repair and extract from copies. Ask before
+  overwriting or deleting any user file, including earlier copies.
+- **Evidence:** label each finding confirmed, hypothesis or unknown. Root-only
+  sources (`/var/db/SystemKeys`, the system TCC database) are unknown unless
+  the user runs the command.
+
+<!-- AI-CONTEXT-END -->
+
+## 1. Triage: compromise or local fault?
+
+Build a timeline before recovering anything. Read-only commands; most need no
+sudo. The aidevops command policy blocks multiline commands, redirection and
+`$` expansion, so use single-line commands with whole-second times.
+
+| Question | Evidence |
+|----------|----------|
+| Who logged in, and when? | `last -30`; `log show --start "<time>" --end "<time>" --predicate 'process == "loginwindow"'` |
+| Was the password rejected or changed? | Same window with `process == "opendirectoryd"`, `"authd"`, `"securityd"`; `MKBUnlockDevice` errors; `dscl . -read` of the user's record, key `accountPolicyData` (`passwordLastSetTime`, `failedLoginCount`) |
+| Did the Mac sleep, wake or reboot? | `pmset -g log` (filter for Wake, Sleep and Shutdown entries); `uptime`; `last reboot` |
+| Was anyone connected remotely? | `screensharingd`, `sshd` and ARD entries in `log show`; `lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN` for ports 22, 5900 and 3283 |
+| Which remote-access agents exist? | `launchctl list`, `/Library/LaunchDaemons`, `/Library/LaunchAgents`, `~/Library/LaunchAgents`; look for TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Splashtop, Acronis/Remotix (`com.nulana.rxagentmac`), ConnectWise, LogMeIn |
+| Unknown accounts or admins? | `dscl . -list /Users UniqueID`; `dscl . -read /Groups/admin GroupMembership`; `sudo fdesetup list` (user runs) |
+| Did an agent session cause it? | Read-only queries of session databases (`reference/memory-lookup.md`) for `security`, `dscl`, `passwd`, `sysadminctl`, keychain paths |
+
+The menu-bar screen-sharing indicator appears for any screen capture,
+including recorders such as ScreenFlow. Ask what was running, and compare with
+System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording.
+
+Before removing a remote-access agent, copy its logs to
+`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/<incident>/`, then use the vendor's
+uninstaller. Ask the user first.
+
+## 2. What a Recovery-mode reset does
+
+- The reset changes the account password without the old one. The login
+  keychain is still encrypted with its own keychain password, which the new
+  account password cannot unlock.
+- At the next login macOS sets the old keychain aside as
+  `~/Library/Keychains/login_renamed_N.keychain-db` and starts a new, empty
+  `login.keychain-db`. Items in the old file are not lost, only locked.
+- The old file opens only with the password it was last rekeyed with. If a
+  fault rewrote it, that may not be any password the user remembers.
+- Agent effects: `gh auth token`, ssh keys saved with `--apple-use-keychain`,
+  commit signing and Chrome Safe Storage fail or prompt. Background routines
+  calling `security find-generic-password` can loop prompts; pause them until
+  the keychain is restored (GH#37232).
+
+## 3. Test passwords safely
+
+- Account password: `dscl . -authonly <user>` (prompts; no output = match).
+  Repeated failures can count towards lockout, so try once per password.
+- Keychain password: copy the file into its own new folder, named exactly
+  `login.keychain-db`, then have the user run
+  `security unlock-keychain <folder>/login.keychain-db`. No output = unlocked.
+  Lock and delete the copy afterwards.
+- Observed on macOS 26 (cause unknown): identical bytes rejected the correct
+  password under another file name and accepted it as `login.keychain-db`.
+  Never conclude a password is wrong from a test on a renamed copy.
+- Never assume which password opens which file. Ask which password was current
+  when that file was last used, and test each candidate separately.
+- Check lock state without a prompt via `SecKeychainGetStatus` (Python
+  `ctypes` against the Security framework), not commands that may trigger
+  SecurityAgent.
+
+## 4. Recover old keychain items
+
+Order of preference:
+
+1. **Old password known:** unlock the set-aside file and move it back, or
+   export items with Keychain Access. To restore it as the login keychain,
+   quit apps, swap the files with a dated backup of the current
+   `login.keychain-db`, restart, and let login rekey it.

Instruct the user to change the restored keychain's password with the known old password, and verify that it unlocks after login, rather than relying on a restart to rekey it. +# Recovery lane: succeed when the last successful refresh is older than
+# STATS_HEALTH_RECOVERY_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h) and the latest attempt did
+# not succeed. Prints the refresh epoch on success.
+_health_repo_needs_recovery() {
+	local slug="$1" runner="$2" epoch attempted age times

Valid; addressed in d014c9ad7b.

With the tree directory still present, `git worktree remove` checks `<tree>/.git` and refuses the tree if it is missing. `_git_directory(target)` also raised first. A resume after Git had already deleted `.git` therefore stayed stranded. That failed closed, but left the retirement incomplete.

- `interrupted_removal.restore_git_link(target, admin)`: when `.git` is absent, it requires the administration directory's `gitdir` backlink to name exactly `<target>/.git`. It then recreates the link (`gitdir: <admin>`) with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`.
- Only journaled resumes call it, after binding the plan's identities. Retirement checks `directory_identity` and `git_identity` (`_restore_private_link`); legacy checks `directory` and `admin_identity` (`_restore_link`). The idle-process census runs first. Afterwards, the existing identity, marker, handle and deletion-only checks run unchanged. Native `git worktree remove` remains the only deleter. `.git` is never listed by `ls-files`, so the restored link is not deletion-only evidence.

Live backlog note: all 27 currently stranded retirements on the affected host still have `tree/.git`. This covers future interruptions, where Git's directory-order deletion removes `.git` first.

Verification: `test_partial_remove_resumes_after_git_deleted_its_link` (retirement, through `cleanup_pass`) and `test_interrupted_removal_resumes_after_git_deleted_its_link` (legacy) both retire the tree and leave no `.lifecycle-retire-*` / `.legacy-retire-*` container.

Same commit, outside-diff boundary findings (`retirement.py:213-224`, `legacy_cleanup.py:153-161`): `validation_boundary()` is taken before the final pre-removal snapshot check, less 1 s for coarse filesystem clocks. It is journaled as `validation_boundary_ns` in the `removing` payload, and `require_deletion_only` compares against it. A `removing` event journaled before this change falls back to the earlier `planned` time, less the same slack. A read-only census of the 27 live stranded trees shows that every remaining Git-visible ctime predates `planned` (27/27), so the fallback does not block the backlog. Tests `test_partial_remove_keeps_data_written_before_removal_was_journaled` and `test_write_before_removal_was_journaled_retains_private_tree` cover a write between the snapshot check and the journal; both now fail closed with `interrupted-removal-content-changed`.

 ```
 
 Inside an OpenCode shell, `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` makes the shell the sender, so replies return to that session. Outside one, the sender is `shell:<user>` and replies go to `outbox/cli/`. `--sender <label>` (1–32 lowercase letters, digits or dashes) names a sessionless sender: origin `cli:<label>`, its own 10-per-minute rate key, and the same trust as any same-user shell. The label is attribution, not authority.
 
+Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 error or refusal; 2 `ask --wait` timeout; 3 a `channel:` target's bound session is not live; 4 `launch` created a session but could not bind, opt in or ask.
+
+### Channel bindings and launch (t18892)
+
+Gateways call these instead of keeping their own room → session maps.
+
+- `bind` writes `bindings/<app>/<channel>.json` (`{ v: 1, app, channel, session_id, actor, server, created_at, updated_at }`). The target is resolved once, at bind time. Binding the same session again is a no-op; a different session replaces it (last atomic write wins; `bindings --json` shows the winner with a computed `live` flag).
+- `<app>` and `<channel>` follow the chat-origin rules (`[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`, `[A-Za-z0-9._:@!#+=-]{1,128}`). A leading `.`, `..` anywhere, `/` or an empty part is rejected.
+- Any `send`, `ask` or `show` target may be `channel:<app>:<channel>`. It resolves only through the binding and only to a live session. If the bound session is not live, the command exits 3 and says so; it never picks another session and never queues for the dead one. The `aidevops_sessions` tool accepts the same targets.
+- `launch` first checks that `--actor` is the verified owner for `chat:<app>:<channel>` (the t18891 rules; the task text is scanned too). Anything else is refused before any server call. It then calls `POST <server>/session` with `{ title }` (and `?directory=` when `--directory` is set; without it the session uses the server's own directory). After the server returns a session ID it writes the binding, sets `chat-wake on` for that session, and sends the text as a chat-origin `ask` from the owner. The server's plugin lists and wakes it like any other session; the reply lands in `outbox/<app>/`.
+- `--server` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:4096`. Plain `http` is accepted only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`; any other host must use `https`. URLs with credentials, a query or a fragment are refused, and so is any redirect from the server. The bus is local files, so the server must run on this host (a remote `opencode serve` needs its own gateway there).
+- Failures: a refused connection creates nothing (exit 1). A timeout, other transport failure, or answer without a usable session ID leaves creation uncertain (exit 1): check the server's session list before retrying to avoid duplicates. Do not assume a server error makes retrying safe either. If bind, opt-in or ask fails after creation, `launch` prints the session ID and exits 4 (`--json`: `session_id`, `failed_step`). The binding is left in place, so `send channel:…` reaches the session on retry; otherwise delete the session on the server.

Valid. Fixed in df04e70692.

The executor owns its tag checkouts until it exits, so lifecycle retirement refuses the mid-run reset (`cleanup_plan.py` `_close_quiescent` → `waiting-for-runs`/`waiting-for-caller`). The same refusal already applied under an inherited interactive owner; this PR made it certain in every context.

- `_full_loop_release_reset_tag_worktree` (`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`): a refused removal no longer fails recovery. The checkout stays registered for post-exit retirement (registry cleanup or the stale reaper), its path is recorded in `_FULL_LOOP_RELEASE_RETAINED_TAG_PATHS`, and `_FULL_LOOP_RELEASE_PATH` is cleared.
- `_full_loop_release_prepare_tag_worktree`: re-preparing a retained PID-named path re-points that tree through the new `_full_loop_release_repoint_tag_worktree` (`full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh`). It does not call `worktree add` on an occupied path. A different tag still gets a fresh tree.
- The repoint only moves a linked tree of this repository with no tracked, untracked or ignored changes, then verifies `HEAD` equals the tag commit. Anything else refuses, so a dirty retained tree still fails closed, as the removal did before.
- Tree names are unchanged, so the reaper regex and the dead-executor reclaim path check keep working.

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift** **`status` coverage check ignores the event union and GitHub's path-matching rules.** `covers($p)` has two independent defects. 1. **The check only looks for `pull_request_target`.** A workflow can add a trigger, such as `issue_comment`, after `apply`. The reference doc says that a narrow list "silently stops those other triggers". `status` is the post-apply verification step, so it must also detect this case. 2. **The check compares `include` entries to the path with exact string equality.** The REST API accepts glob patterns and `~ALL` in `include`. An empty `include` array includes all workflows not matched by an excluded pattern. A policy without `conditions` targets all workflows. An admin can add a valid glob or `~ALL` policy, and `status` still returns 1. Security posture and sync then report a false `UNCOVERED`. Check every declared event of each workflow. Accept an empty `include`, a missing `include` and `~ALL`. Real glob matching needs a glob-to-regex conversion. At minimum, report glob includes as "unverified" so they do not count as uncovered.

+readonly POLICY_RULE_TYPE="restrict_action_events"
+_T="true"
+readonly WORKFLOW_DIR=".github/workflows"
+readonly REPOS_JSON_DEFAULT="${HOME}/.config/aidevops/repos.json"
+
+# Populated by _policy_scan: JSON {default_branch, public, workflows:[{path,events,parsed}]}
+_POLICY_SCAN_JSON=""
+
+_policy_error() {
+	local message="$1"
+	printf 'actions-event-policy: %s\n' "$message" >&2
+	return 1
+}
+
+_policy_usage() {
+	cat <<'USAGE'
+Usage:
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh status --repo OWNER/REPO
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh plan   --repo OWNER/REPO
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh apply  --repo OWNER/REPO
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh status|plan --all-managed
+
+status: exit 0 when covered or not applicable (private/internal repo or no
+        pull_request_target workflow), exit 1 when uncovered, exit 2 on error.
+plan:   print the exact policy JSON body (read-only).
+apply:  create or update the policy named aidevops-pull-request-target-gates.
+        Refuses when a targeted workflow's events cannot be parsed.
+USAGE
+	return 0
+}
+
+_policy_require_dependencies() {
+	local dependency=""
+	for dependency in gh jq yq base64; do
+		if ! command -v "$dependency" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+			_policy_error "missing dependency: ${dependency}"
+			return 1
+		fi
+	done
+	return 0
+}
+
+_policy_validate_repo() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	if [[ ! "$repo_slug" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; then
+		_policy_error "repository must be OWNER/REPO"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	return 0

+	jq -ce '
+		if type == "string" then [.]
+		elif type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string") then .
+		elif type == "object" then keys
+		else error("unsupported on:") end
+		| unique | select(length > 0)' <<<"$on_json" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+	return 0
+}
+
+# Print "true" when the workflow calls a local reusable workflow.
+_policy_calls_local_reusable() {
+	local content="$1"
+	local result=""
+	result=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" |
+		yq -o=json '[.jobs[]? | .uses // "" | select(type == "!!str" and test("^\\./"))] | length > 0' 2>/dev/null) || result="false"
+	printf '%s\n' "$result"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_policy_fetch_file() {
+	local slug="$1"
+	local path="$2"
+	local ref="$3"
+	gh api --method GET -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" \
+		"repos/${slug}/contents/${path}?ref=${ref}"
+	return $?
+}
+
+# Scan the default branch. Sets _POLICY_SCAN_JSON.
+_policy_scan() {
+	local slug="$1"
+	local repo_json="" default_branch="" visibility="" listing="" path="" content=""
+	local events="" parsed="" reusable="" entries="[]"
+	repo_json=$(_policy_api_read "repos/${slug}") || {
+		_policy_error "cannot read repository ${slug}"
+		return 1
+	}

+	visibility=$(jq -r '.visibility // (if .private then "private" else "public" end)' <<<"$repo_json")
+	if [[ -z "$default_branch" ]]; then
+		_policy_error "cannot determine default branch for ${slug}"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	listing=$(_policy_api_read "repos/${slug}/contents/${WORKFLOW_DIR}?ref=${default_branch}" 2>/dev/null) || listing="[]"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn
+# Plan, apply and verify the repository Actions event policy that allows
+# `pull_request_target` for the workflow files that declare it.
+#
+# GitHub blocks `pull_request_target` by default in public repositories from
+# 2026-12-02 (brownouts 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-16, 16:00-18:00 UTC) unless an
+# applicable Actions policy explicitly allows it.
+# https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-02-pull_request_target-blocked-by-default-december-2
+#
+# Usage:
+#   actions-event-policy-helper.sh status --repo OWNER/REPO
+#   actions-event-policy-helper.sh plan   --repo OWNER/REPO
+#   actions-event-policy-helper.sh apply  --repo OWNER/REPO
+#   actions-event-policy-helper.sh status|plan --all-managed
+#
+# status exits 0 when covered or not applicable, 1 when uncovered, 2 on error.
+# plan and status are read-only. apply is explicit and per repository.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)" || exit 1
+# shellcheck source=shared-constants.sh
+source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-constants.sh"
+
+readonly POLICY_NAME="aidevops-pull-request-target-gates"
+readonly POLICY_EVENT="pull_request_target"
+readonly POLICY_API_VERSION="2026-03-10"
+readonly POLICY_RULE_TYPE="restrict_action_events"
+_T="true"
+readonly WORKFLOW_DIR=".github/workflows"
+readonly REPOS_JSON_DEFAULT="${HOME}/.config/aidevops/repos.json"
+
+# Populated by _policy_scan: JSON {default_branch, public, workflows:[{path,events,parsed}]}
+_POLICY_SCAN_JSON=""
+
+_policy_error() {
+	local message="$1"
+	printf 'actions-event-policy: %s\n' "$message" >&2
+	return 1
+}
+
+_policy_usage() {
+	cat <<'USAGE'
+Usage:
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh status --repo OWNER/REPO
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh plan   --repo OWNER/REPO
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh apply  --repo OWNER/REPO
+  actions-event-policy-helper.sh status|plan --all-managed
+
+status: exit 0 when covered or not applicable (private/internal repo or no
+        pull_request_target workflow), exit 1 when uncovered, exit 2 on error.
+plan:   print the exact policy JSON body (read-only).
+apply:  create or update the policy named aidevops-pull-request-target-gates.
+        Refuses when a targeted workflow's events cannot be parsed.
+USAGE
+	return 0
+}
+
+_policy_require_dependencies() {
+	local dependency=""
+	for dependency in gh jq yq base64; do
+		if ! command -v "$dependency" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+			_policy_error "missing dependency: ${dependency}"
+			return 1
+		fi
+	done
+	return 0
+}
+
+_policy_validate_repo() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	if [[ ! "$repo_slug" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; then
+		_policy_error "repository must be OWNER/REPO"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	return 0
+}
+
+_policy_api_read() {
+	local endpoint="$1"
+	gh api --method GET -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: ${POLICY_API_VERSION}" "$endpoint"
+	return $?
+}
+
+# Print the sorted, de-duplicated events declared in a workflow's `on:` key,
+# one JSON array. Uses a real YAML parser (yq): PyYAML-style loaders read the
+# key `on` as boolean true. Exit 1 when the events cannot be parsed.
+_policy_parse_events() {
+	local content="$1"
+	local on_json=""
+	on_json=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | yq -o=json '.on' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+	jq -ce '
+		if type == "string" then [.]
+		elif type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string") then .
+		elif type == "object" then keys
+		else error("unsupported on:") end
+		| unique | select(length > 0)' <<<"$on_json" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+	return 0
+}
+
+# Print "true" when the workflow calls a local reusable workflow.
+_policy_calls_local_reusable() {
+	local content="$1"
+	local result=""
+	result=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" |
+		yq -o=json '[.jobs[]? | .uses // "" | select(type == "!!str" and test("^\\./"))] | length > 0' 2>/dev/null) || result="false"
+	printf '%s\n' "$result"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_policy_fetch_file() {
+	local slug="$1"
+	local path="$2"
+	local ref="$3"
+	gh api --method GET -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" \
+		"repos/${slug}/contents/${path}?ref=${ref}"
+	return $?
+}
+
+# List the workflow directory. Sets _POLICY_LISTING. A confirmed 404 (directory
+# absent) is an empty list; any other failure (403, rate limit, 5xx, network) is
+# an error so status never reports success on an unchecked repository.
+_policy_list_workflows() {
+	local slug="$1"
+	local branch="$2"
+	local err_file="" err_text=""
+	err_file=$(mktemp) || {
+		_policy_error "cannot create temp file"
+		return 1
+	}
+	if _POLICY_LISTING=$(_policy_api_read "repos/${slug}/contents/${WORKFLOW_DIR}?ref=${branch}" 2>"$err_file"); then
+		rm -f "$err_file"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	err_text=$(cat "$err_file")
+	rm -f "$err_file"
+	# gh api prints the status as the trailing "(HTTP NNN)" of its error line.
+	if grep -Eq '^gh: .*\(HTTP 404\)[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$err_text"; then
+		_POLICY_LISTING="[]"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	_policy_error "cannot list ${WORKFLOW_DIR} in ${slug}"
+	return 1
+}
+
+# Scan the default branch. Sets _POLICY_SCAN_JSON.
+_policy_scan() {
+	local slug="$1"
+	local repo_json="" default_branch="" visibility="" listing="" path="" content=""
+	local events="" parsed="" reusable="" entries="[]"
+	repo_json=$(_policy_api_read "repos/${slug}") || {
+		_policy_error "cannot read repository ${slug}"
+		return 1
+	}
+	default_branch=$(jq -r '.default_branch // empty' <<<"$repo_json")
+	visibility=$(jq -r '.visibility // (if .private then "private" else "public" end)' <<<"$repo_json")
+	if [[ -z "$default_branch" ]]; then
+		_policy_error "cannot determine default branch for ${slug}"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	_policy_list_workflows "$slug" "$default_branch" || return 1
+	listing="$_POLICY_LISTING"
+	while IFS= read -r path; do
+		[[ -n "$path" ]] || continue
+		case "$path" in
+		"${WORKFLOW_DIR}"/*.yml | "${WORKFLOW_DIR}"/*.yaml) ;;
+		*) continue ;;
+		esac
+		content=$(_policy_fetch_file "$slug" "$path" "$default_branch") || {
+			_policy_error "cannot read ${path} in ${slug}"
+			return 1
+		}
+		# Only files that mention the event matter; others are never targeted.
+		if ! grep -q "$POLICY_EVENT" <<<"$content"; then
+			continue
+		fi
+		if events=$(_policy_parse_events "$content"); then
+			parsed="$_T"
+			if [[ "$(_policy_calls_local_reusable "$content")" == "$_T" ]]; then
+				events=$(jq -c '. + ["workflow_call"] | unique' <<<"$events")
+			fi
+		else
+			parsed="false"
+			events="[]"
+		fi
+		# A mention in a comment or string is not a declaration.
+		if [[ "$parsed" == "$_T" ]] && ! jq -e --arg e "$POLICY_EVENT" 'index($e) != null' <<<"$events" >/dev/null; then
+			continue
+		fi
+		entries=$(jq -c --arg p "$path" --argjson e "$events" --argjson ok "$parsed" \
+			'. + [{path:$p, events:$e, parsed:$ok}]' <<<"$entries")
+	done < <(jq -r '.[]? | select(.type == "file") | .path' <<<"$listing" | LC_ALL=C sort)
+	_POLICY_SCAN_JSON=$(jq -cn --arg b "$default_branch" --arg v "$visibility" --argjson w "$entries" \
+		'{default_branch:$b, visibility:$v, public:($v == "public"), workflows:$w}')
+	return 0
+}
+
+# Print the policy body for the scan in _POLICY_SCAN_JSON.
+_policy_build_body() {
+	jq -ce --arg name "$POLICY_NAME" --arg rule "$POLICY_RULE_TYPE" '
+		{
+			name: $name,
+			enforcement: "active",
+			conditions: {workflow_path: {include: [.workflows[].path], exclude: []}},
+			rules: [{type: $rule, parameters: {allowed_events: ([.workflows[].events[]] | unique)}}]
+		}' <<<"$_POLICY_SCAN_JSON"
+	return $?
+}
+
+# Print uncovered workflow paths, one per line, given the policies JSON.
+_policy_uncovered_paths() {
+	local policies_json="$1"
+	jq -r --arg ev "$POLICY_EVENT" --arg rule "$POLICY_RULE_TYPE" --argjson pol "$policies_json" '
+		def globre: gsub("(?<c>[.+^${}()|\\[\\]\\\\])"; "\\\(.c)")
+			| gsub("\\*\\*"; "\^A") | gsub("\\*"; "[^/]*") | gsub("\^A"; ".*")
+			| "^" + . + "$";
+		def matches($p): . == "~ALL" or . == $p or ($p | test(globre));

+# Stdout: rotated newline-separated slugs
+# Returns 0 always.

+	local slugs="$2"
+	local last_slug="" slug="" before="" after="" seen=0
+	if [[ -f "$cursor_file" ]]; then

+			after="${after}${slug}"$'\n'
+			continue
+		fi
+		before="${before}${slug}"$'\n'
+		if [[ "$slug" == "$last_slug" ]]; then
+			seen=1
+		fi
+	done <<<"$slugs"

+	return 0

+# the even-spacing schedule, and only while the available share is at least

+DELIVERY_FLOOR_DIVISOR = 4

+	[[ "$ttl" -ge 1 && "$ttl" -le 720 ]] || return 1
+	if [[ -n "$version" ]] && ! _mrh_valid_version "$version"; then
+		printf 'Invalid release version: expected [v]X.Y.Z with optional prerelease/build suffixes\n' >&2
+		return 1
+	fi
+	local existing="" rc=0 existing_pr="" dups="" now="" expires="" json="" mode="create"
+	existing=$(_mrh_active_hold "$repo") || rc=$?
+	case "$rc" in
+	0)
+		existing_pr=$(jq -r '.pr // empty' <<<"$existing")
+		if [[ "$existing_pr" != "$pr" ]]; then
+			printf 'Refused: hold for release PR #%s is already active (owner_session=%s)\n' \
+				"$existing_pr" "$(jq -r '.owner_session // "unknown"' <<<"$existing")" >&2
+			return 1
+		fi
+		mode="$_MRH_UPDATE"
+		;;
+	3) _mrh_read "$repo" "$_MRH_HOLD_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1 && mode="$_MRH_UPDATE" || true ;;
+	*)
+		printf 'WARNING: cannot read manual release hold for %s; not holding\n' "$repo" >&2
+		return 1
+		;;
+	esac
+	if [[ -n "$version" ]]; then
+		dups=$(_mrh_duplicate_prs "$repo" "$version" "$pr") || dups=""
+		if [[ -n "$dups" ]]; then
+			printf 'Refused: release %s already has open PR(s): %s\n' "$version" "$(tr '\n' ' ' <<<"$dups")" >&2
+			return 1
+		fi
+	fi
+	now=$(_mrh_now)
+	expires=$((now + ttl * 60))
+	json=$(jq -cn --arg repo "$repo" --argjson pr "$pr" --arg version "$version" --arg owner "$(_mrh_session_id)" \
+		--arg created "$(_mrh_iso "$now")" --arg exp "$(_mrh_iso "$expires")" --argjson expe "$expires" \
+		'{repository:$repo,pr:$pr,version:$version,owner_session:$owner,created_at:$created,expires_at:$exp,expires_at_epoch:$expe}') || return 1
+	rc=0
+	_mrh_write "$repo" "$_MRH_HOLD_REF" "$json" "$mode" || rc=$?
+	if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+		printf 'Refused: could not record hold\n' >&2
+		return 1
+	fi
+	if [[ "$mode" == "$_MRH_UPDATE" ]]; then
+		printf 'WARNING: hold update is advisory; concurrent updates may overwrite it\n' >&2
+	fi
+	printf 'MANUAL_RELEASE_HOLD_SET repo=%s release_pr=%s expires_at=%s\n' "$repo" "$pr" "$(_mrh_iso "$expires")"
+	return 0
+}
+
+cmd_unhold() {
+	local repo="${1:-}"
+	_mrh_valid_repo "$repo" || return 1
+	local rc=0
+	_mrh_read "$repo" "$_MRH_HOLD_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
+	if [[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]]; then
+		printf 'No manual release hold for %s\n' "$repo"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	_mrh_delete "$repo" "$_MRH_HOLD_REF" || {
+		printf 'Could not delete hold ref for %s\n' "$repo" >&2
+		return 1
+	}
+	printf 'MANUAL_RELEASE_HOLD_RELEASED repo=%s\n' "$repo"
+	return 0
+}
+
+cmd_status() {
+	local repo="${1:-}"
+	_mrh_valid_repo "$repo" || return 1
+	local json="" rc=0
+	json=$(_mrh_active_hold "$repo") || rc=$?
+	case "$rc" in
+	0) printf '%s\n' "$json" ;;
+	3) printf 'No active manual release hold for %s\n' "$repo" ;;
+	*)
+		printf 'Hold unreadable for %s\n' "$repo" >&2
+		return 1
+		;;
+	esac
+	return 0
+}
+
+cmd_owner() {
+	local repo="${1:-}"
+	local tag="${2:-}"
+	shift 2 || true
+	local session=""
+	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+		case "${1:-}" in
+		--session)
+			session="${2:-}"
+			shift 2
+			;;
+		*) return 1 ;;
+		esac
+	done
+	local part=""
+	part=$(_mrh_tag_ref_part "$tag") || return 1
+	_mrh_valid_repo "$repo" && [[ "$session" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$ ]] || {
+		printf 'Usage: aidevops release owner OWNER/REPO TAG --session ID\n' >&2
+		return 1
+	}
+	local ref="${_MRH_OWNER_PREFIX}/${part}" mode="create" rc=0 json=""
+	_mrh_read "$repo" "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 && mode="$_MRH_UPDATE" || true
+	json=$(jq -cn --arg repo "$repo" --arg tag "$tag" --arg s "$session" --arg at "$(_mrh_iso "$(_mrh_now)")" \
+		'{repository:$repo,tag:$tag,session:$s,recorded_at:$at}') || return 1
+	_mrh_write "$repo" "$ref" "$json" "$mode" || rc=$?
+	[[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || return 1
+	printf 'MANUAL_RELEASE_OWNER repo=%s tag=%s session=%s\n' "$repo" "$tag" "$session"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# Best-effort bus notice to the recorded roll-out owner. Never fails the caller.
+cmd_owner_notify() {
+	local repo="${1:-}"
+	local tag="${2:-}"
+	shift 2 || true
+	local result="release run and update test finished"
+	[[ "${1:-}" != "--result" ]] || result="${2:-$result}"
+	local part="" json="" session="" text=""
+	part=$(_mrh_tag_ref_part "$tag") || return 1
+	_mrh_valid_repo "$repo" || return 1
+	json=$(_mrh_read "$repo" "${_MRH_OWNER_PREFIX}/${part}") || {
+		printf 'No roll-out owner recorded for %s %s\n' "$repo" "$tag"
+		return 0
+	}
+	session=$(jq -r '.session // empty' <<<"$json")
+	[[ "$session" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$ ]] || return 0
+	text="Release ${tag} of ${repo}: ${result}. You own the roll-out."
+	if command -v aidevops >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+		timeout 5 aidevops sessions send "$session" "$text" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+## Interactive TUI Restart for Maintenance
+
+Long-lived OpenCode TUIs hold `opencode.db`, which blocks archive/VACUUM, and they keep an old plugin until they restart. Use `opencode-session-restart-helper.sh` (GH#37663) to interrupt, maintain and resume them:
+
+- `aidevops opencode-db maintenance-window --restart-interactive [--yes]` drains headless workers and then runs the helper's `stop`. When maintenance ends, or fails, `resume` runs as a cleanup. For other work (plugin, runtime or OS upgrades) use `opencode-session-restart-helper.sh run [--yes] -- <command…>`. `inventory [--json]` lists holders with PID, session ID, cwd, age, busy/idle state and tmux/screen pane.
+- `stop` sends each busy session a session-bus message, delivered at its next tool result, asking it to save its continuation checkpoint (see "Context Compaction Resilience") and pause. It waits up to `OPENCODE_RESTART_WAIT_TIMEOUT` (600s). A busy session is never signalled; it is skipped and reported. An idle session (no activity for `OPENCODE_RESTART_IDLE_SECONDS`, default 120) gets SIGTERM with no escalation. Before the signal, its `{session_id, cwd, pane, argv, resume_command}` goes into `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-session-restart/manifest.json`.
+- `resume` runs `cd <cwd> && opencode -s <id>` in the original tmux pane (`send-keys`) or screen window (`stuff`). Bare-TTY sessions can't be reattached, so they keep the resume command in the manifest and in the session-start notice. Every resumed session gets a session-bus note: it was restarted, and it should load its checkpoint and revalidate state before the next side effect.
+- Authority: an operator at a terminal confirms the stop or passes `--yes`. A run without a terminal (scheduler, headless agent) only notifies owners, at most once per 24h per session. The exception is a host whose config allows unattended stops (`allow_unattended=true` in `~/.config/aidevops/opencode-session-restart.conf`, e.g. a runner host with no human TUIs). Scheduled `auto` runs notify holders after `AUTO_SKIP_ESCALATION_COUNT` holder-blocked skips.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn

+# opencode-session-restart-helper.sh — safe interrupt → maintain → resume for
+# long-lived interactive OpenCode TUI sessions (GH#37663).
+#
+# Interactive TUIs left open for days hold opencode.db, so archive/VACUUM and
+# plugin/runtime upgrades never run. This helper:
+#   1. inventories interactive holders (session-bus presence `kind: tui`, plus
+#      activity heartbeats for DB holders that predate the session bus);
+#   2. asks busy sessions over the session bus to checkpoint and pause;
+#   3. waits for idle and never signals a busy session;
+#   4. stops idle TUIs gracefully (SIGTERM) and records a restart manifest;
+#   5. after maintenance, relaunches `opencode -s <id>` in the original
+#      tmux/screen pane, or leaves a resume command for bare-TTY sessions.
+#
+# Authority: stopping is opt-in. A terminal operator confirms (or passes
+# --yes). Without a terminal (scheduler, headless agent) the helper only
+# notifies owners unless the host config allows unattended restarts.
+#
+# Usage: opencode-session-restart-helper.sh <command> [options]
+#   inventory [--json] [--all]       Interactive holders: pid, session, cwd, age, busy/idle, pane
+#   stop [options]                   Checkpoint request → wait idle → SIGTERM idle TUIs → manifest
+#   resume                           Relaunch stopped sessions from the manifest
+#   run [options] -- <command…>      stop, run the command, then always resume
+#   notify [--reason <text>]         Session-bus note to holders (throttled, never stops)
+#   notice                           One session-start line for sessions awaiting manual resume
+#   help
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 error; 2 some sessions skipped (busy, unverifiable or
+# still running after the signal); 3 notify-only (no stop authority).

+	print_info() { printf '[INFO] %s\n' "$*"; return 0; }
+	print_success() { printf '[OK] %s\n' "$*"; return 0; }
+	print_warning() { printf '[WARN] %s\n' "$*"; return 0; }
+	print_error() { printf '[ERROR] %s\n' "$*" >&2; return 0; }
+fi

+readonly RESTART_STATE_DIR="${OPENCODE_RESTART_STATE_DIR:-${HOME}/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-session-restart}"
+readonly RESTART_MANIFEST="${RESTART_STATE_DIR}/manifest.json"
+readonly RESTART_NOTIFIED_DIR="${RESTART_STATE_DIR}/notified"
+readonly RESTART_PRESENCE_DIR="${AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR:-${HOME}/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/session-bus}/presence"
+readonly RESTART_DB="${OPENCODE_DB_PATH:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/share}/opencode/opencode.db}"
+readonly RESTART_HOST_CONF="${OPENCODE_RESTART_HOST_CONF:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-${HOME}/.config}/aidevops/opencode-session-restart.conf}"
+readonly RESTART_SENDER="opencode-maintenance"
+readonly RESTART_DEFAULT_REASON="maintenance"
+readonly RESTART_SESSION_RE='^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$'
+readonly RESTART_MANIFEST_MAX_AGE=604800

+: "${OPENCODE_RESTART_POLL:=10}"            # seconds between idle polls
+: "${OPENCODE_RESTART_IDLE_SECONDS:=120}"   # quiet period after last activity before a stop
+: "${OPENCODE_RESTART_EXIT_TIMEOUT:=30}"    # seconds to wait for exit after the signal
+: "${OPENCODE_RESTART_SIGNAL:=TERM}"
+: "${OPENCODE_RESTART_OPENCODE_BIN:=opencode}"

+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Process facts

+_uint_or() {

+	local fallback="$2"

+# _pid_alive <pid> — live and not a zombie.
+_pid_alive() {

+_pid_args() {

+	local args first rest

+	first="${first##*/}"

+	rest=" ${args#"${args%% *}"} "

+	lstart=$(printf '%s' "$lstart" | tr -s '[:space:]' ' ')
+	lstart="${lstart# }"
+	lstart="${lstart% }"
+	[[ -z "$lstart" ]] || printf 'ps:%s' "$lstart"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _pid_verified <pid> <start_token> — still the same interactive OpenCode process.
+_pid_verified() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local token="$2"
+	_pid_alive "$pid" || return 1
+	_pid_is_interactive_opencode "$pid" || return 1
+	if [[ "$token" == ps:* ]]; then
+		[[ "$(_pid_start_token "$pid")" == "$token" ]] || return 1
+	fi
+	return 0
+}
+
+_pid_env_value() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local name="$2"
+	local file="/proc/${pid}/environ"
+	[[ -r "$file" ]] || return 0
+	tr '\0' '\n' <"$file" 2>/dev/null | awk -v key="${name}=" 'index($0, key) == 1 { print substr($0, length(key) + 1); exit }' || true
+	return 0
+}
+
+_pid_cwd() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local cwd=""
+	if [[ -e "/proc/${pid}/cwd" ]]; then
+		cwd=$(readlink "/proc/${pid}/cwd" 2>/dev/null || true)
+	elif command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then

+	fi
+	printf '%s' "$cwd"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_pid_age_seconds() {

+	local now started
+	now=$(date +%s)
+	started=$(OPENCODE_DB_PS_COMMAND="$OPENCODE_RESTART_PS" _opencode_db_holder_start_epoch "$pid" "$now")
+	if [[ "$started" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then printf '%s' "$((now - started))"; else printf '0'; fi
+	return 0
+}
+

+# screen or tty. tmux: TMUX_PANE from the environment (Linux), else the
+# process ancestry matched against `tmux list-panes -a`.
+_pane_locate() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local pane tmux_env sty window
+	pane=$(_pid_env_value "$pid" TMUX_PANE)
+	tmux_env=$(_pid_env_value "$pid" TMUX)
+	if [[ "$pane" =~ ^%[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+		printf 'tmux%s%s%s%s\n' "$SEP" "$pane" "$SEP" "${tmux_env%%,*}"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	sty=$(_pid_env_value "$pid" STY)
+	window=$(_pid_env_value "$pid" WINDOW)

+		printf 'screen%s%s%s%s\n' "$SEP" "$window" "$SEP" "$sty"
+		return 0

+		return 0
+	fi
+	printf 'tty%s%s%s\n' "$SEP" "$("$OPENCODE_RESTART_PS" -o tty= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]' || true)" "$SEP"

+_pane_from_tmux_ancestry() {

+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

+# _db_holder_pids — PIDs holding the active DB; "*" when the DB filter does not

+	return 0

+# _row <field…> — print one SEP-delimited row.
+_row() {
+	local IFS="$SEP"
+	printf '%s\n' "$*"
+	return 0

+# _heartbeat_row <pid> — fallback row from the activity heartbeat for a DB

+_heartbeat_row() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local dir file fields busy last sessions count
+	dir=$(opencode_db_activity_dir)
+	for file in "$dir/${pid}"-*.json; do
+		[[ -f "$file" ]] || continue

+_inventory_rows() {

+	local holders pid sid status cwd last token source seen=" " kind target socket

+		[[ -n "$pid" && "$seen" != *" ${pid} "* ]] || continue

+		[[ "$sid" =~ $RESTART_SESSION_RE ]] || continue
+		IFS="$SEP" read -r kind target socket < <(_pane_locate "$pid")
+		_row "$pid" "$sid" "$status" "$cwd" "$last" "$token" "$source" "$(_pid_age_seconds "$pid")" "$kind" "$target" "$socket"
+	done <<<"$holders"
+	return 0

+cmd_inventory() {
+	local json=false all=false arg rows pid sid status cwd age kind target
+	for arg in "$@"; do
+		case "$arg" in
+		--json) json=true ;;
+		--all) all=true ;;
+		*) print_error "Unknown inventory option: $arg"; return 1 ;;
+		esac
+	done
+	if [[ "$json" == true ]] && ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+		printf '[]\n'
+		return 0
+	fi
+	rows=$(_inventory_rows "$all")

+		printf '%s\n' "$rows" | jq -R -s -c '[split("\n")[] | select(length > 0) | split("\^_")
+			| {pid: (.[0] | tonumber), session_id: .[1], status: .[2], cwd: .[3], last_activity_epoch: (.[4] | tonumber? // 0),
+			   source: .[6], age_seconds: (.[7] | tonumber? // 0), pane_kind: .[8], pane: .[9]}]'
+		return 0
+	fi
+	if [[ -z "$rows" ]]; then
+		print_info "No interactive OpenCode TUI holders found"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	printf '%-8s %-32s %-5s %-7s %-6s %s\n' PID SESSION STATE AGE PANE CWD
+	while IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid status cwd _ _ _ age kind target _; do
+		printf '%-8s %-32s %-5s %-7s %-6s %s\n' "$pid" "$sid" "$status" "$((age / 3600))h" "${kind}${target:+:$target}" "$cwd"

+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Manifest
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

+_manifest_read() {
+	if [[ -f "$RESTART_MANIFEST" ]] && jq -e '.entries | type == "array"' "$RESTART_MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+		jq -c '.' "$RESTART_MANIFEST"
+	else
+		printf '{"v":1,"entries":[]}'
+	fi
+	return 0

+# _manifest_write <json> — atomic replace; drops entries older than 7 days.
+_manifest_write() {
+	local json="$1"
+	local tmp cutoff
+	mkdir -p "$RESTART_STATE_DIR"
+	cutoff=$(($(date +%s) - RESTART_MANIFEST_MAX_AGE))
+	tmp=$(mktemp "${RESTART_STATE_DIR}/manifest.XXXXXX")
+	if ! jq --argjson cutoff "$cutoff" '.entries |= map(select((.stopped_epoch // 0) >= $cutoff))' <<<"$json" >"$tmp"; then

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Reject empty JSON in `_manifest_write`. Otherwise the helper can wipe the manifest and still signal the session.** `_stop_one` runs inside an `if` (`_stop_targets`), so `set -e` is ignored there. Suppose `entry=$(jq -nc ...)` fails and returns empty. Then `_manifest_put` runs `jq --argjson e ""`, which fails, and `json` is empty. `_manifest_write ""` runs `jq` on whitespace-only input. That produces no output and exits 0. The empty temp file replaces `manifest.json`. `_manifest_put` returns success, so `_stop_one` sends the signal. Two results follow: - The session has no resume record. - Earlier entries are lost, because an empty manifest reads back as `entries: []`. Require non-empty JSON before the write. Also require that `jq` produced output.
🛡️ Proposed fix

```diff --- "a/.agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh" +++ "b/.agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh" @@ -355,11 +355,12 @@ # _manifest_write — atomic replace; drops entries older than 7 days. _manifest_write() { local json="$1" local tmp cutoff + [[ -n "${json//[[:space:]]/}" ]] || { print_error "Refusing to write an empty restart manifest"; return 1; } mkdir -p "$RESTART_STATE_DIR" cutoff=$(($(date +%s) - RESTART_MANIFEST_MAX_AGE)) tmp=$(mktemp "${RESTART_STATE_DIR}/manifest.XXXXXX") - if ! jq --argjson cutoff "$cutoff" '.entries |= map(select((.stopped_epoch // 0) >= $cutoff))' <<<"$json" >"$tmp"; then + if ! jq --argjson cutoff "$cutoff" '.entries |= map(select((.stopped_epoch // 0) >= $cutoff))' <<<"$json" >"$tmp" || [[ ! -s "$tmp" ]]; then rm -f "$tmp" return 1 fi ```
As per path instructions, `.agents/scripts/*.sh` must have "Error recovery mechanisms".

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Fix the infinite loop when an option is missing its value.** `_parse_stop_args` is called as `_parse_stop_args "$@" || return 1`. In that context `set -e` is ignored. ** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Re-check that a session is still idle immediately before the signal.** `quiet` is a snapshot taken once, at the end of `_wait_for_quiet`. `_stop_one` then runs one session at a time. Each call can wait up to `OPENCODE_RESTART_EXIT_TIMEOUT` seconds in `_wait_for_exit`. `_stop_one` re-verifies only the PID identity and start token. It does not re-check the busy/idle state. +_pane_from_tmux_ancestry() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local panes="" depth=0 cur="$pid" match=""
+	command -v "$OPENCODE_RESTART_TMUX_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+	panes=$("$OPENCODE_RESTART_TMUX_BIN" list-panes -a -F '#{pane_pid} #{pane_id}' 2>/dev/null || true)
+	[[ -n "$panes" ]] || return 0
+	while [[ "$cur" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ && "$cur" -gt 1 && "$depth" -lt 20 ]]; do
+		match=$(awk -v p="$cur" '$1 == p { print $2; exit }' <<<"$panes")
+		if [[ "$match" =~ ^%[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+			printf '%s' "$match"
+			return 0
+		fi
+		cur=$("$OPENCODE_RESTART_PS" -o ppid= -p "$cur" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]' || true)
+		depth=$((depth + 1))
+	done
+	return 0
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Inventory
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# _db_holder_pids — PIDs holding the active DB; "*" when the DB filter does not
+# apply (no DB, no lsof) so every live TUI is a candidate.
+_db_holder_pids() {
+	local files=() rc=0 out=""
+	[[ -f "$RESTART_DB" ]] && command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf '*'; return 0; }
+	files=("$RESTART_DB")
+	[[ ! -e "${RESTART_DB}-wal" ]] || files+=("${RESTART_DB}-wal")
+	[[ ! -e "${RESTART_DB}-shm" ]] || files+=("${RESTART_DB}-shm")
+	out=$(lsof -t "${files[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
+	if [[ "$rc" -gt 1 ]]; then printf '*'; return 0; fi
+	printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk 'NF' | sort -u
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _presence_rows — one SEP-delimited row per live TUI pid:
+# pid, session_id, status (idle|busy), directory, last_activity_epoch, start_token, source
+_presence_rows() {
+	local file records=""
+	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+	[[ -d "$RESTART_PRESENCE_DIR" ]] || return 0
+	for file in "$RESTART_PRESENCE_DIR"/*.json; do
+		[[ -f "$file" ]] || continue
+		records+=$(jq -c 'select(type == "object" and .kind == "tui" and (.pid | type) == "number" and (.session_id | type) == "string")' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+		records+=$'\n'
+	done
+	[[ -n "${records//[[:space:]]/}" ]] || return 0
+	printf '%s' "$records" | jq -rs '
+		group_by(.pid)[] | (max_by(.updated_epoch // 0)) as $r
+		| [($r.pid | tostring), $r.session_id,
+		   (if all(.[]; .status == "idle") then "idle" else "busy" end),
+		   ($r.directory // ""), (($r.last_activity_epoch // 0) | tostring),
+		   ($r.start_token // ""), "presence"] | map(tostring | gsub("[\^_\n]"; " ")) | join("\^_")' 2>/dev/null || true
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _row <field…> — print one SEP-delimited row.
+_row() {
+	local IFS="$SEP"
+	printf '%s\n' "$*"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _heartbeat_row <pid> — fallback row from the activity heartbeat for a DB
+# holder without session-bus presence. Requires exactly one open session.
+_heartbeat_row() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local dir file fields busy last sessions count
+	dir=$(opencode_db_activity_dir)
+	for file in "$dir/${pid}"-*.json; do
+		[[ -f "$file" ]] || continue
+		fields=$(jq -r '[(.busy_sessions // "" | tostring), (.last_activity_epoch // "" | tostring)] | join(" ")' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+		read -r busy last <<<"$fields"
+		sessions=$(jq -r '.sessions[]? | strings' "$file" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NF' || true)
+		count=$(printf '%s\n' "$sessions" | awk 'NF' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
+		[[ "$busy" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$last" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$count" -eq 1 ]] || continue
+		_row "$pid" "$sessions" "$([[ "$busy" -eq 0 ]] && printf idle || printf busy)" "$(_pid_cwd "$pid")" "$last" "" heartbeat
+		return 0
+	done
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _inventory_rows [all] — verified interactive holders as TSV rows (see
+# _presence_rows) with age, pane kind, pane target and pane socket appended.
+_inventory_rows() {
+	local all="${1:-false}"
+	local holders pid sid status cwd last token source seen=" " kind target socket
+	holders='*'
+	[[ "$all" == true ]] || holders=$(_db_holder_pids)
+	while IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid status cwd last token source; do
+		[[ -n "$pid" && "$sid" =~ $RESTART_SESSION_RE ]] || continue
+		if [[ "$holders" != '*' ]] && ! grep -qx "$pid" <<<"$holders"; then continue; fi
+		_pid_verified "$pid" "$token" || continue
+		seen+="${pid} "
+		[[ -n "$cwd" ]] || cwd=$(_pid_cwd "$pid")
+		IFS="$SEP" read -r kind target socket < <(_pane_locate "$pid")
+		_row "$pid" "$sid" "$status" "$cwd" "$last" "$token" "$source" "$(_pid_age_seconds "$pid")" "$kind" "$target" "$socket"
+	done < <(_presence_rows)
+	[[ "$holders" != '*' ]] || return 0
+	while IFS= read -r pid; do
+		[[ -n "$pid" && "$seen" != *" ${pid} "* ]] || continue
+		_pid_verified "$pid" "" || continue
+		IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid status cwd last token source < <(_heartbeat_row "$pid") || continue
+		[[ "$sid" =~ $RESTART_SESSION_RE ]] || continue
+		IFS="$SEP" read -r kind target socket < <(_pane_locate "$pid")
+		_row "$pid" "$sid" "$status" "$cwd" "$last" "$token" "$source" "$(_pid_age_seconds "$pid")" "$kind" "$target" "$socket"
+	done <<<"$holders"
+	return 0
+}
+
+cmd_inventory() {
+	local json=false all=false arg rows pid sid status cwd age kind target
+	for arg in "$@"; do
+		case "$arg" in
+		--json) json=true ;;
+		--all) all=true ;;
+		*) print_error "Unknown inventory option: $arg"; return 1 ;;
+		esac
+	done
+	if [[ "$json" == true ]] && ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+		printf '[]\n'
+		return 0
+	fi
+	rows=$(_inventory_rows "$all")
+	if [[ "$json" == true ]]; then
+		printf '%s\n' "$rows" | jq -R -s -c '[split("\n")[] | select(length > 0) | split("\^_")
+			| {pid: (.[0] | tonumber), session_id: .[1], status: .[2], cwd: .[3], last_activity_epoch: (.[4] | tonumber? // 0),
+			   source: .[6], age_seconds: (.[7] | tonumber? // 0), pane_kind: .[8], pane: .[9]}]'
+		return 0
+	fi
+	if [[ -z "$rows" ]]; then
+		print_info "No interactive OpenCode TUI holders found"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	printf '%-8s %-32s %-5s %-7s %-6s %s\n' PID SESSION STATE AGE PANE CWD
+	while IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid status cwd _ _ _ age kind target _; do
+		printf '%-8s %-32s %-5s %-7s %-6s %s\n' "$pid" "$sid" "$status" "$((age / 3600))h" "${kind}${target:+:$target}" "$cwd"
+	done <<<"$rows"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Manifest
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_manifest_read() {
+	if [[ -f "$RESTART_MANIFEST" ]] && jq -e '.entries | type == "array"' "$RESTART_MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+		jq -c '.' "$RESTART_MANIFEST"
+	else
+		printf '{"v":1,"entries":[]}'
+	fi
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _manifest_write <json> — atomic replace; drops entries older than 7 days.
+_manifest_write() {
+	local json="$1"
+	local tmp cutoff
+	mkdir -p "$RESTART_STATE_DIR"
+	cutoff=$(($(date +%s) - RESTART_MANIFEST_MAX_AGE))
+	tmp=$(mktemp "${RESTART_STATE_DIR}/manifest.XXXXXX")
+	if ! jq --argjson cutoff "$cutoff" '.entries |= map(select((.stopped_epoch // 0) >= $cutoff))' <<<"$json" >"$tmp"; then
+		rm -f "$tmp"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	chmod 600 "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || true
+	mv -f "$tmp" "$RESTART_MANIFEST"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _manifest_put <entry-json> — upsert by session_id.
+_manifest_put() {
+	local entry="$1"
+	local json
+	json=$(_manifest_read | jq -c --argjson e "$entry" '.entries = ([.entries[] | select(.session_id != $e.session_id)] + [$e])')
+	_manifest_write "$json"
+	return $?
+}
+
+_manifest_set_status() {
+	local sid="$1"
+	local status="$2"
+	local json
+	json=$(_manifest_read | jq -c --arg s "$sid" --arg st "$status" --argjson now "$(date +%s)" \
+		'.entries |= map(if .session_id == $s then .status = $st | .updated_epoch = $now else . end)')
+	_manifest_write "$json"
+	return $?
+}
+
+_resume_command() {
+	local cwd="$1"
+	local sid="$2"
+	local cmd=""
+	[[ -z "$cwd" ]] || cmd="cd -- $(printf '%q' "$cwd") && "
+	printf '%s%s -s %s' "$cmd" "$OPENCODE_RESTART_OPENCODE_BIN" "$(printf '%q' "$sid")"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Session-bus messages
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_bus_send() {
+	local sid="$1"
+	local text="$2"
+	[[ -x "$OPENCODE_RESTART_SESSION_BUS_HELPER" ]] || command -v "$OPENCODE_RESTART_SESSION_BUS_HELPER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
+	printf '%s' "$text" | "$OPENCODE_RESTART_SESSION_BUS_HELPER" send "$sid" --sender "$RESTART_SENDER" - >/dev/null 2>&1
+	return $?
+}
+
+_checkpoint_request_text() {
+	local reason="$1"
+	printf 'OpenCode maintenance (%s) will restart this TUI so the session DB can be archived/compacted. At your next safe pause: save a continuation checkpoint (session-checkpoint-helper.sh save, or /checkpoint) per reference/session.md "Context Compaction Resilience", then stop and stay idle. The session is relaunched with opencode -s after maintenance; a busy session is never stopped.' "$reason"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_resumed_note_text() {
+	local reason="$1"
+	local when="$2"
+	printf 'This session was stopped at %s for OpenCode maintenance (%s) and relaunched with opencode -s. Load your continuation checkpoint (session-checkpoint-helper.sh load) and revalidate git, PR and tool state before the next side effect.' "$when" "$reason"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Authority
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_host_allows_unattended() {
+	[[ "${OPENCODE_RESTART_ALLOW_UNATTENDED:-}" == 1 || "${OPENCODE_RESTART_ALLOW_UNATTENDED:-}" == true ]] && return 0
+	[[ -f "$RESTART_HOST_CONF" ]] || return 1
+	grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*allow_unattended[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*(true|1)[[:space:]]*$' "$RESTART_HOST_CONF"
+	return $?
+}
+
+# _authorize_stop <yes> <count> — 0 stop allowed, 3 notify-only, 1 declined.
+_authorize_stop() {
+	local yes="$1"
+	local count="$2"
+	local answer=""
+	if [[ -t 0 ]]; then
+		[[ "$yes" == true ]] && return 0
+		read -r -p "Checkpoint, stop and later resume ${count} interactive OpenCode session(s)? [y/N] " answer || answer=""
+		[[ "$answer" =~ ^[Yy]([Ee][Ss])?$ ]] && return 0
+		print_info "Declined; no session was stopped"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	if [[ "$yes" == true ]] && _host_allows_unattended; then
+		return 0
+	fi
+	print_warning "No terminal confirmation and host config does not allow unattended restarts (${RESTART_HOST_CONF}: allow_unattended=true); notifying owners only"
+	return 3
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# stop
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_row_is_quiet() {
+	local status="$1"
+	local last="$2"
+	local now
+	now=$(date +%s)
+	[[ "$status" == idle ]] || return 1
+	last=$(_uint_or "$last" 0)
+	((now - last >= OPENCODE_RESTART_IDLE_SECONDS)) || return 1
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _current_row <pid> <rows> — fresh inventory row for one pid.
+_current_row() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local rows="$2"
+	awk -F"$SEP" -v p="$pid" '$1 == p { print; exit }' <<<"$rows"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _wait_for_quiet <targets> — poll until each target is quiet or the timeout
+# passes; print the final rows of targets that went quiet.
+_wait_for_quiet() {
+	local targets="$1"
+	local all="$2"
+	local waited=0 rows pid row status last pending
+	local poll
+	poll=$(_uint_or "$OPENCODE_RESTART_POLL" 10)
+	[[ "$poll" -gt 0 ]] || poll=1
+	while true; do
+		rows=$(_inventory_rows "$all")
+		pending=0
+		while IFS="$SEP" read -r pid _rest; do
+			[[ -n "$pid" ]] || continue
+			row=$(_current_row "$pid" "$rows")
+			IFS="$SEP" read -r _ _ status _ last _ <<<"$row"
+			[[ -n "$row" ]] && ! _row_is_quiet "$status" "$last" && pending=$((pending + 1))
+		done <<<"$targets"
+		if [[ "$pending" -eq 0 || "$waited" -ge "$OPENCODE_RESTART_WAIT_TIMEOUT" ]]; then
+			break
+		fi
+		print_info "  waiting for ${pending} busy session(s) to reach a safe pause (${waited}s/${OPENCODE_RESTART_WAIT_TIMEOUT}s)" >&2
+		sleep "$poll"
+		waited=$((waited + poll))
+	done
+	while IFS="$SEP" read -r pid _rest; do
+		[[ -n "$pid" ]] || continue
+		row=$(_current_row "$pid" "$rows")
+		IFS="$SEP" read -r _ _ status _ last _ <<<"$row"
+		if [[ -n "$row" ]] && _row_is_quiet "$status" "$last"; then printf '%s\n' "$row"; fi
+	done <<<"$targets"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_wait_for_exit() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local waited=0
+	while _pid_alive "$pid" && [[ "$waited" -lt "$OPENCODE_RESTART_EXIT_TIMEOUT" ]]; do
+		sleep 1
+		waited=$((waited + 1))
+	done
+	_pid_alive "$pid" && return 1
+	return 0
+}
+
+# _stop_one <row> <reason> — record the manifest entry, signal, confirm exit.
+_stop_one() {
+	local row="$1"
+	local reason="$2"
+	local pid sid status cwd last token source age kind target socket entry
+	IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid status cwd last token source age kind target socket <<<"$row"
+	if ! _pid_verified "$pid" "$token"; then
+		print_warning "Session ${sid}: PID ${pid} changed before stop; skipped"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	entry=$(jq -nc --arg sid "$sid" --argjson pid "$pid" --arg cwd "$cwd" --arg kind "$kind" --arg pane "$target" \
+		--arg socket "$socket" --arg argv "$(_pid_args "$pid")" --arg resume "$(_resume_command "$cwd" "$sid")" \
+		--arg reason "$reason" --argjson now "$(date +%s)" --argjson age "$(_uint_or "$age" 0)" \
+		'{session_id: $sid, pid: $pid, cwd: $cwd, pane_kind: $kind, pane: $pane, pane_socket: $socket, argv: $argv,
+		  resume_command: $resume, reason: $reason, age_seconds: $age, stopped_epoch: $now, updated_epoch: $now, status: "stopping"}')
+	_manifest_put "$entry" || { print_error "Cannot write restart manifest; not stopping ${sid}"; return 1; }
+	kill "-${OPENCODE_RESTART_SIGNAL}" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+	if _wait_for_exit "$pid"; then
+		_manifest_set_status "$sid" stopped
+		print_success "Stopped idle session ${sid} (PID ${pid}, ${kind}${target:+ ${target}})"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	_manifest_set_status "$sid" stop_failed
+	print_warning "Session ${sid} (PID ${pid}) still running ${OPENCODE_RESTART_EXIT_TIMEOUT}s after SIG${OPENCODE_RESTART_SIGNAL}; left running"
+	return 1
+}
+
+_parse_stop_args() {
+	STOP_YES=false
+	STOP_ALL=false
+	STOP_REASON="$RESTART_DEFAULT_REASON"
+	STOP_SESSIONS=""
+	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+		local arg="$1"
+		case "$arg" in
+		--yes | -y) STOP_YES=true; shift ;;
+		--all) STOP_ALL=true; shift ;;
+		--reason) STOP_REASON="${2:-$RESTART_DEFAULT_REASON}"; shift 2 ;;
+		--session) STOP_SESSIONS+=" ${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
+		--wait-timeout) OPENCODE_RESTART_WAIT_TIMEOUT=$(_uint_or "${2:-}" "$OPENCODE_RESTART_WAIT_TIMEOUT"); shift 2 ;;
+		--) shift; STOP_REST=("$@"); return 0 ;;
+		*) print_error "Unknown option: $arg"; return 1 ;;
+		esac
+	done
+	STOP_REST=()
+	return 0
+}
+
+cmd_stop() {
+	STOP_REST=()
+	_parse_stop_args "$@" || return 1
+	_stop_targets
+	return $?
+}
+
+# _stop_targets — body of stop using the parsed STOP_* options.
+_stop_targets() {
+	local rows targets="" row pid sid status last quiet skipped=0 stopped=0 auth=0
+	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { print_error "jq is required"; return 1; }
+	rows=$(_inventory_rows "$STOP_ALL")
+	while IFS= read -r row; do
+		[[ -n "$row" ]] || continue
+		IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid _ <<<"$row"
+		[[ -z "$STOP_SESSIONS" || " ${STOP_SESSIONS} " == *" ${sid} "* ]] || continue
+		targets+="${row}"$'\n'
+	done <<<"$rows"
+	if [[ -z "$targets" ]]; then
+		print_info "No interactive OpenCode TUI holders to restart"
+		return 0
+	fi
+	_authorize_stop "$STOP_YES" "$(printf '%s' "$targets" | awk 'NF' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" || auth=$?
+	if [[ "$auth" -eq 3 ]]; then
+		_notify_rows "$targets" "$STOP_REASON"
+		return 3
+	fi
+	[[ "$auth" -eq 0 ]] || return 1
+	# Only busy sessions get the checkpoint request: an idle session is already
+	# at a safe pause, and a queued message would arrive only after the resume.
+	while IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid status _; do
+		[[ -n "$pid" ]] || continue
+		if [[ "$status" != idle ]]; then
+			_bus_send "$sid" "$(_checkpoint_request_text "$STOP_REASON")" ||
+				print_warning "Session ${sid}: checkpoint request not delivered (session bus unavailable)"
+			print_info "Session ${sid} (PID ${pid}) is busy; asked it to checkpoint and pause"
+		fi
+	done <<<"$targets"
+	quiet=$(_wait_for_quiet "$targets" "$STOP_ALL")
+	while IFS="$SEP" read -r pid sid _; do
+		[[ -n "$pid" ]] || continue
+		if [[ -z "$(_current_row "$pid" "$quiet")" ]]; then
+			if ! _pid_alive "$pid"; then
+				print_info "Session ${sid} (PID ${pid}) exited on its own; nothing to resume"
+				continue
+			fi
+			print_warning "Session ${sid} (PID ${pid}) stayed busy; not stopped"
+			skipped=$((skipped + 1))
+			continue
+		fi
+		if _stop_one "$(_current_row "$pid" "$quiet")" "$STOP_REASON"; then
+			stopped=$((stopped + 1))
+		else
+			skipped=$((skipped + 1))
+		fi
+	done <<<"$targets"
+	print_info "Interactive restart: ${stopped} stopped, ${skipped} skipped. Manifest: ${RESTART_MANIFEST}"
+	[[ "$skipped" -eq 0 ]] || return 2
+	return 0
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# resume
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_session_live() {
+	local sid="$1"
+	local file="${RESTART_PRESENCE_DIR}/${sid}.json"
+	local pid token
+	[[ -f "$file" ]] || return 1
+	pid=$(jq -r '.pid // empty' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+	token=$(jq -r '.start_token // empty' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+	_pid_verified "$pid" "$token"
+	return $?
+}
+
+_tmux() {
+	local socket="$1"
+	shift
+	if [[ -n "$socket" ]]; then
+		"$OPENCODE_RESTART_TMUX_BIN" -S "$socket" "$@"
+	else
+		"$OPENCODE_RESTART_TMUX_BIN" "$@"
+	fi
+	return $?
+}
+
+# _relaunch_entry <entry-json> — print the new status for one manifest entry.
+_relaunch_entry() {
+	local entry="$1"
+	local sid kind pane socket cmd
+	sid=$(jq -r '.session_id' <<<"$entry")
+	kind=$(jq -r '.pane_kind // "tty"' <<<"$entry")
+	pane=$(jq -r '.pane // ""' <<<"$entry")
+	socket=$(jq -r '.pane_socket // ""' <<<"$entry")
+	cmd=$(jq -r '.resume_command' <<<"$entry")
+	if _session_live "$sid"; then
+		printf 'already_running'
+		return 0
+	fi
+	case "$kind" in
+	tmux)
+		if _tmux "$socket" display-message -p -t "$pane" '#{pane_id}' >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
+			_tmux "$socket" send-keys -t "$pane" -l "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
+			_tmux "$socket" send-keys -t "$pane" Enter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+			printf 'resumed'
+			return 0

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Check that the target pane is at a shell prompt before typing the resume command.** `_relaunch_entry` only checks that the pane ID still exists. Maintenance can take a long time. By then the pane may run something else, for example `vim`, a REPL or another TUI. In that case `send-keys -l "$cmd"` followed by `Enter` types `cd … && opencode -s …` into that program. The same applies to the `screen` branch. The status is still recorded as `resumed`. Query `#{pane_current_command}` through `display-message`. Send the keys only when it is a known shell. Otherwise fall back to `pending_manual`.
